name: Mitt Romney
role: U.S. senator from Utah (2019-2025), governor of Massachusetts (2003-2007) and 2012 Republican presidential nominee
summary: Romney is a business-oriented Republican who favors free enterprise, lower and simpler taxes, balanced budgets, school choice, a strong military and alliances, and restricting abortion except for rape, incest and the mother's life. He has been a critic of Donald Trump and voted to convict him twice, and in the Senate worked across the aisle on infrastructure and gun safety while backing a child cash benefit and, late in his career, higher taxes on the wealthy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: As governor he signed a 2006 law that required residents to hold insurance and reached near-universal coverage, but he opposed the federal Affordable Care Act, wanted repeal and replacement with state-led, market-based plans, and in 2018 still defended state-based plans. His Senate agenda focuses on cost transparency, not state-provided coverage.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: In 2023 he introduced the Higher Wages for American Workers Act, which would raise the federal minimum wage gradually to $11, index it, and mandate E-Verify; in 2016 he said it was time for an increase. In 2012 he had favored only moderate, indexed raises.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In the 2012 debate he said that in his experience the private sector typically provides a better product at lower cost than government, and he built his convention case on free enterprise creating prosperity rather than redistributing it.

public-ownership.rationale: He wanted government to sell its GM stock quickly, argued against a federal bailout of Detroit in favor of a managed private bankruptcy, and repeatedly criticized government picking industrial winners and losers; no support for public ownership of utilities or rail is recorded.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: His Senate site says fair means higher-income people pay higher rates, and in a December 2025 New York Times essay (as reported by Wikipedia) he called for the affluent to contribute more, including lifting the payroll-tax cap and limiting step-up in basis on mega-estates. This reverses his 2012 plan for across-the-board cuts; the most recent position is used, and reported secondhand here.

unions-good.rationale: He opposed the Employee Free Choice Act, backed stripping public-employee bargaining rights, blamed teachers' unions for school failure, and in 2008 urged the UAW to end adversarial labor relations, while acknowledging unions once brought workers security and better pay.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In the 2012 debate he said regulation is essential but can become excessive, and he promised to repeal Dodd-Frank and cut regulation; as senator he signed letters against new Biden-era rules, though he also sponsored a crypto anti-money-laundering bill and vaping limits.

cut-welfare.rationale: His Senate site criticizes Democratic plans for universal pre-K and free community college as making Americans more dependent on Washington, and in 2012 he opposed loosening welfare-to-work rules; but his Family Security Act would instead consolidate programs into a monthly child cash benefit, so the evidence is mixed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: As governor in 2005 he suggested wiretapping mosques and monitoring foreign students to improve counterterrorism intelligence, and he supported the Patriot Act; he opposed SOPA as intrusive.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He said in 2007 he would fight legalization of marijuana 'tooth and nail' and later opposed legalizing recreational or medical marijuana; by 2018 he accepted strictly regulated medical marijuana, but no support for legal recreational use is recorded.

empower-police-military.rationale: He called for a military 'second to none' and for large increases in troop numbers and a defense spending floor of 4 percent of GDP; his record also includes tough-on-crime sentencing laws, though he joined a 2020 march against police brutality.

decide-locally.rationale: His Senate site says authority over education should return to the states, that gun laws and school safety are for states, and that public land decisions need state and local approval; in 2012 he argued health care and disaster relief should rest with states.

traditional-family.rationale: He calls himself pro-family, names strong families as one of three pillars of national strength, and his Family Security Act aims to promote marriage; he opposed same-sex marriage for most of his career.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Mixed: he opposed same-sex marriage and civil unions throughout his 2002-2012 campaigns and backed a federal marriage amendment, but in 2022 he voted for the Respect for Marriage Act, which codified same-sex and interracial marriage recognition in federal law.

abortion-legal.rationale: His Senate site says he opposes abortion except in cases of rape, incest or to protect the mother's life, and he cosponsored a 20-week ban; he describes himself as pro-life since 2005.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Points both ways: he calls for ending chain migration and the visa lottery and strongly opposes illegal immigration, but praises legal immigration, proposed more visas for skilled workers in 2012, and wants a merit-based legal system.

free-trade.rationale: His Senate site says he supports free and fair trade, opposes broad-based tariffs, and he voted for USMCA; he has said protectionist policies eventually fail, while saying trade deals must benefit workers hurt by past trade.

nation-first.rationale: His Senate platform stresses linking arms with friends and allies to confront China and leading 'the free world'; he rejected tariff-driven unilateralism in 2016 even as he insisted on American exceptionalism.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He backed a no-fly zone in Libya, urged arming the Syrian opposition against Assad's crackdown, and as senator calls for holding China accountable for atrocities against the Uyghurs.

open-borders.rationale: His Senate site calls for a physical barrier on the southern border, mandatory E-Verify and full enforcement of immigration law, and says he strongly opposes illegal immigration.

limit-growth.rationale: His platforms are built around growth: a 12-million-job plan in 2012 and, as senator, a focus on competitiveness and innovation; he opposed mandatory emission caps because of their cost.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He says climate change needs bipartisan action and joined the Climate Solutions Caucus, but wants it to come mainly through private-sector innovation and carbon capture; he opposed mandatory emission limits in 2012 and signed a letter opposing stricter fuel-economy rules.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He supported building more nuclear plants in 2012, and his Senate site names small modular nuclear among technologies he supports funding.

central-planning.rationale: He criticized government picking winners in solar and wind (Solyndra) and called Obama's approach 'trickle-down government', arguing that private enterprise creates prosperity.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In 2012 he proposed eliminating the estate tax, but in December 2025 he wrote that mega-estates over $100 million should lose step-up in basis; this is a narrow limit, not heavy taxation of large inheritances.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: His Senate site says he opposes broad-based tariffs but will support focused tariffs on well-documented cheaters; in 2016 he said a 35 percent tariff would start a trade war that would hurt workers.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Mixed: he attacked Obama's clean-energy loans for picking winners and losers, but he backed the CHIPS and Science Act, called for substantially more federal basic research, and promoted the 2021 infrastructure bill.

military-superiority.rationale: His Senate platform says a military 'second to none' is critical, and in 2012 he proposed adding at least 100,000 troops and setting defense spending at 4 percent of GDP.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He said in the 2012 debate that this is a nation of immigrants and welcomes legal immigrants, and in 2016 he condemned Trump for scapegoating Muslims and Mexican immigrants.

equal-outcomes.rationale: At the 2012 convention he contrasted the free-enterprise system 'creating tomorrow's prosperity' with 'trying to redistribute today's'; his debate plan stressed opportunity and jobs, not leveling.

taxation-theft.rationale: He treats taxation as a legitimate tool: his Senate page describes a fair system where higher earners pay higher rates, and he has proposed and defended specific tax plans throughout his career.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In December 2011 he pledged to reaffirm as a vital national interest Israel's existence as a Jewish state, and he repeatedly described Israel as America's best friend in the Middle East.

school-vouchers.rationale: He has long supported vouchers, charters and school choice; at the 2012 convention he said every parent should have a choice, and in 2024 he joined a resolution to designate National School Choice Week.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: His Senate site says there is no excuse for a trillion-dollar deficit, he voted against the 2021 American Rescue Plan, and he campaigned on a balanced budget; he had backed Obama's 2009 stimulus in January 2009, but later called it wasteful.

work-for-welfare.rationale: In 2012 his campaign opposed the Obama administration's plan to give states flexibility on welfare-to-work rules, and he spoke of the 'dignity of work' for mothers on welfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: His 2008 op-ed called for ending the enmity between labor and management, with profit sharing for employees and cooperation to restructure the auto industry.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: In 2012 he promised to double drilling permits, approve Keystone XL and 'like coal'; as senator he says fossil fuels will keep a role and supports Utah's oil and gas output while backing methane-leak fixes.

national-mission.rationale: His writing and speeches stress American exceptionalism and leadership of the free world; he said America has freed other nations from dictators, but he also told Afghans to win their own independence.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His record endorses active government roles beyond defense and justice: he signed a near-universal health insurance law, negotiated the infrastructure bill, proposed a federal child cash benefit, and supports federal research funding.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He voted in 2022 to advance the Respect for Marriage Act, which protects interracial marriages as well as same-sex marriages.

party-controls-media.rationale: He vowed to veto any revival of the Fairness Doctrine and in 2016 criticized Trump for applauding the prospect of twisting the Constitution to limit freedom of the press.

death-penalty.rationale: As governor he proposed legislation to reinstate the death penalty for terrorism, killing of police, torture murders and multiple killings, with strict DNA-evidence standards; it failed in the Massachusetts House.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He has said he has always fought for abstinence education and supported abstinence-focused programs, though he also backed teaching marriage and family before childbearing.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: As governor and afterward he said the science class is for evolution and that intelligent design belongs in a religion or philosophy class, and he opposed teaching it in public school science classes.

restrict-pornography.rationale: He called pornography a 'cesspool', proposed a filter on new computers in 2008, and vowed in 2012 to enforce anti-pornography laws vigorously, while saying he was not trying to stop adults' access.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Mixed: he opposed the contraception mandate for religious employers and backed Fairness for All's exemptions, but opposed Arizona's SB 1062 religious refusal bill.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: His Senate platform says modernizing the nuclear deterrent must remain a high priority, including the Ground Based Strategic Deterrent missile program.

flat-income-tax.rationale: His Senate tax page states a fair system means higher-income individuals pay a higher rate than lower-income individuals.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His impeachment speech argued a president can commit acts so egregious that, even without a statutory crime, they require removal, and that the Constitution makes the Senate try a president.

no-bailouts.rationale: His 2008 op-ed argued against a federal bailout of the Detroit automakers, saying the bailout would guarantee their demise and that a managed bankruptcy was better; he also said Italy should not be bailed out. He did support federal backing for a managed restructuring.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: He voted for USMCA, which his Senate site says raised labor standards.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: As governor he eliminated the state Office of Affirmative Action.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: In 2014 he urged Arizona's governor to veto SB 1062, which would have let businesses refuse service to gay customers on religious grounds, and he backed state anti-discrimination protections for LGBT workers.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He voted to convict Trump in 2020 and 2021, saying a president who corrupts an election commits an appalling abuse of public trust that justifies removal under the Constitution.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He said he would reverse the policy against arming moderate Syrian rebels, calling Obama's response too slow.

corporate-influence.rationale: He supported the Citizens United decision and criticized McCain-Feingold, but said he wished money could be taken out of politics and called for more disclosure; in 2016 he decried the Clintons' 'crony capitalism'.

non-intervention.rationale: He supported the Iraq invasion, regime change pressure on Iran, the Libyan no-fly zone and arming Syrian rebels, and said military action against Iran was a real option.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: His Senate Family Security Act is explicitly designed to promote marriage, and he has campaigned for legal protections for marriage as one man and one woman.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: At the 2012 convention he credited the American free-enterprise system with harnessing creativity and industry to create prosperity, and said he believes in free enterprise in his 2025 essay.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He frames the American free-enterprise system as the basis for prosperity and has never advocated a third way.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He signed gay-pride proclamations as governor, backed domestic partnership benefits and state anti-discrimination laws, and in 1994 said equality for gays and lesbians should be a mainstream concern.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He attacked Trump in 2016 for cheering assaults on protesters and for wanting to limit press freedom, and in 2020 voted to convict a president for corrupting an election.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Mixed: he praised the Fairness for All Act, which would bar discrimination against LGBT people, but in 2021 opposed the Biden rule allowing transgender girls in girls' sports.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He said in 2016 that insulting all Muslims keeps them from helping fight ISIS, and as senator pressed the FBI director about violence against Muslims and Jews; he supports equality for Muslims.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: His platforms call for a military 'second to none', more troops and higher defense spending.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He calls for linking arms with allies against China and said in 2022 that countries must choose between the West and Russia, not both.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: He supported Don't Ask, Don't Tell in 2007 but said in December 2011 that he would not reverse its repeal.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: His record includes the death penalty proposal, three-strikes sentencing, mandatory sentences and privately run state prisons; he marched against police brutality in 2020 but never proposed abolishing either.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: In June 2024 he proposed a framework with Senators Reed, Moran and King to mitigate existential risk from artificial general intelligence.

abolish-ip.rationale: His Senate health page says drug-price policy should not sacrifice companies' intellectual property, and as a candidate he campaigned against Chinese intellectual-property theft.

anonymous-payments.rationale: He sponsored the CANSEE Act in 2023 to require decentralized-finance services to meet anti-money-laundering and sanctions rules.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He supported the 2003 Iraq invasion and the troop surge, argued for preparing military strikes on Iran, and backed the Libyan no-fly zone.

free-public-college.rationale: His Senate page calls Democratic proposals for free community college an unnecessary expansion of bureaucracy, and he opposes blanket student-loan forgiveness.

future-generations.rationale: His Senate energy page says it is imperative that America do its part to protect the planet for future generations.

arms-reduction.rationale: He opposed New START, doubted Reagan's goal of abolishing nuclear weapons, and called for enlarging the military and modernizing the nuclear force.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He supported Wisconsin and Ohio laws that stripped public employees' collective-bargaining rights and opposed card-check recognition, but wanted labor-management negotiation to restructure the auto industry.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: He signed the cut, cap and balance pledge, still favors a Balanced Budget Amendment, and co-sponsors a Fiscal Stability Act commission to rein in the debt.

student-debt-relief.rationale: His Senate page says he will vigorously oppose blanket student loan forgiveness as unfair to those who paid.

farm-price-support.rationale: Mixed: he backed ethanol subsidies in 2011 but said in Iowa he would not promise handouts, and his 1994 campaign called for cutting farm subsidies.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: His Senate platform says modernizing the nuclear deterrent must remain a high priority while adversaries pursue nuclear ambitions, and he opposed New START.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: He supported three-strikes sentencing, mandatory sentence increases for repeat drunk drivers, and mandatory sentencing in his 1994-2002 campaigns.

close-ties-china.rationale: His Senate page calls China's quest to be the leading power the central challenge of the century and urges confronting its predatory policies with allies; in 2012 he vowed to label China a currency manipulator.

multipolar-world.rationale: He describes America as the leader of the free world and favors peace through strength, and ranks Russia and China as principal rivals.

notes: Positions shifted over time and the most recent clear one is used: pro-choice-leaning in 1994-2002 but pro-life since 2005; opposed same-sex marriage until 2012 but voted for the Respect for Marriage Act in 2022; backed 2009 stimulus but opposed it in 2012; favored higher taxes on the wealthy in December 2025 (read only via Wikipedia's summary of a New York Times essay). Several 2007-2012 positions (Guantanamo, enhanced interrogation, DADT, marijuana) have no recent restatement. The book No Apology was not available as full text.
